answer: Each agent must post a bond locked on-chain before its actions count toward votes or rewards; slashing rules seize that bond if the agent is caught double-voting or violating a challenge. This makes a swarm of fake identities costly: an attacker must fund a separate bond for every Sybil and risks losing each one, rather than creating identities for free. A harbor operator can require the same rule for entry, while onyx and opal accounts face identical terms.
